the GDOFs of the interference channel and the relay channel are balanced by the optimum power allocation.

the achievable generalized degrees of freedoms (GDOF), which is the asymptotically optimal degrees of freedom (DoF), is the maximum of the GDOF achieved by the interference channel ( IC) part and the GDOF obtained by the orthogonal relay channel( ORC) part, and the power allocation that maximizes the GDOF is affected by the parameters of the channel.

the GDOFs of ICOR is maximized by the power allocation that balances the GDOF gains of the IC part of ICOR and the ORC parts of ICOR, and the optimum power allocations depend on the channel parameters of ICOR.

the GDOF analysis of the ICOR, which is a new model and has potential applications in wireless communications.
the GDOF performance of ICOR, which is a new model that combines the IC and ORC.
the achievable GDOFs of the ICOR and the optimum power allocations at the source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GDOFs of the IC part, the ORC part and the whole system are all determined by the power allocation at the source and the channel parameters.
, the GDOF is the sum of the GDOF achieved in the IC part and ORC part.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the achievable GDOFs of ICOR is determined by the channel parameters, the power allocation at the source and the channel parameters of ICOR.
the GDOFs of ICOR can be maximized by the power allocation at the source, where the optimum power allocation depends on the channel parameters.
the achievable GDOFs of the whole system, the IC part and ORC part are all affected by the channel parameter and power allocation scheme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the achievable GDOFs of the IC and the ORC are both affected by the channel parameter of the source-to-relay channel.
we have shown that the GDOFs of the IC part can be balanced by the GDOFs in the ORC part.
the power allocation scheme for the GDOF maximization is different from the power allocation scheme that is used to maximize the sum-rate.
